tapeLine: US stocks rose Monday: the S&P 500 gained 0.7% to 7,773.95, the Nasdaq Composite 1.1% to a record 27,477.31, the Dow 90.94 points (0.2%) to 51,267.90 and the Russell 2000 0.5% to 2,847.14, per the Associated Press. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.315%, a 52-week high, and the 30-year 5.670%, per Sharecast. Tuesday premarket levels were not sourced this session.
matters:
Stocks rose with yields at multi-year highs. The ISM services PMI for September came in at 54.9, roughly in line with expectations and modestly below August, while its prices index rose 1.4 points to 74, the highest 12-month average since March 2023, per Sharecast.

The Nasdaq set a record led by Nvidia, per Sharecast and Yahoo Finance. The September FOMC minutes arrive Wednesday; the next FOMC meeting is 28 October.

Invalidation: the tone of Wednesday's FOMC minutes, whether the 10-year keeps rising above 5.3%, and the services prices index at 74.
alsoOnTape: Oil and gold are not carried: no dated, consistent levels were found this session.

Rates — 10-year at a 52-week high of 5.315% after Friday's weak payrolls (+29K); FOMC is 28 October.
Fed calendar — September minutes Wednesday; Williams and Bowman speak Tuesday, per Newsquawk.
flow: The Nasdaq closed at a record Monday, per the Associated Press; the S&P 500 ended near its record, per the Associated Press.

regime.tag: Stocks and the Nasdaq rose to a record while the 10-year hit a 52-week high.
regime.sizing: Equities are absorbing higher yields; Wednesday's FOMC minutes are the next evidence.

secondOrder: Equities rose as the 10-year yield and the ISM prices index both rose. That is an observation, not a forecast.

Yesterday's brief listed whether the 10-year holds above 5.2% as a test. It held and rose to 5.315%, per Sharecast.
